Hi team — attaching a compact technical summary and a diagram (kvm-segmentation-diagram.pdf) that covers the operational controls Michael requested. Key points below — please pull whichever you need into your DPF packet.

1) KMS and key separation
- Customer-managed keys supported: customers may supply an external KMS key or bring their own key (BYOK) integrated via our KMS connectors.
- Key hierarchy: per-tenant DEK (data encryption key) wrapped by a per-tenant KEK stored in the integrated KMS/HSM. Master keys never leave the HSM in wrapped form.
- HSM: we support customer HSMs via standard KMIP-compatible endpoints or cloud-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys.
- Rotation: KEKs rotate according to customer SLA (default 90 days) with automated rewrap and documented key rotation runbooks.

2) KV cache semantics (inference runtime)
- Cache contents: KV cache stores transformer attention key/value blobs (ephemeral inference state) for in-flight sessions only. No persistent user PII is stored in cache; we explicitly do not cache raw user-uploaded documents or file attachments.
- Encryption: all cache shards are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3). When CMK is enabled, KV cache disk volumes are encrypted using customer KEK-wrapped DEKs.
- TTL and eviction: KV cache entries follow strict TTLs based on session type (default session TTL = 5 minutes; configurable per-customer) and LRU eviction. Logs show only opaque cache keys; cache contents are not retained beyond TTL and are zeroed on eviction.
- Access controls: runtime enforces IAM policies; only runtime processes with verified attestation can read cache shards. Access is logged and auditable.

3) Request routing / cross-border controls
- Routing policies: we support policy-driven routing rules: region-only (requests must remain in specified cloud region), region-preferred with fallback, and cost-priority. Policies are enforced at the edge routing layer.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to compatible model variant or alternate capacity is possible but only within the configured policy. If a tenant requests region-only, fallback across regions is disabled.
- Proof and evidence: we can export routing audit traces (per-request route id + region) for the retention period in the DPA.

Assumptions and limitations:
- If customer chooses hosted default keys (Redwood-managed), key material may be resident in our cloud KMS with HSM. BYOK provides the strongest separation but requires customer KMS availability for key operations.
- KV cache behavior applies to token-level inference state; application-level persistent stores (e.g., embeddings DB) are separate and subject to customer configuration.

I've attached kvm-segmentation-diagram.pdf and a one-page CV of the runtime's cache lifecycle. Happy to present these in a short technical call.

Best — Karthik

Michael — I've prepared a DPA Annex redline focused on the items Aurora called out and included granular operational commitments where we can provide them. Key legal-ops bullets below; redline attached (DPA_Annex_Redline_Aurora_v1.docx):

- Key custody: we offer a CMK option with explicit contractual language that keys are customer-controlled; default (Redwood-managed) keys are described and limited to non-production demonstration use unless otherwise agreed.
- Audit logs & access: Redwood will provide per-request routing traces and access logs for the retention period in section X; logs include anonymized request ids and routing metadata; we will not include full prompt text in routing traces unless agreed in a scoped engagement.
- KV cache: we will include a clause that cache is ephemeral, TTL-limited, encrypted at rest/in transit, and that Redwood will not use cache contents for model improvement absent a separate opt-in.
- Cross-border restrictions: contractual option to require region-only execution for the tenant, with agreed SLAs and documented fallback behavior.

Next steps: please review the redline and mark any items you need tightened. If Aurora legal wants to discuss a bespoke retention or audit scope, we can schedule a call with compliance and infra.

Regards — Kimberly

--
